models.comments: Source rate $0.15/hour = $0.0025/minute (base rate, excludes add-ons such as diarization or entity detection). Converted to $/k seconds: 0.0025 * 1000 / 60 ~= 0.041667.

models.name: Universal-3.5 Pro (async)
models.comments: Source rate $0.21/hour, "Universal-3.5 Pro" under the Pre-recorded Speech-to-Text API tab. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.21 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.0583333 recurring, stored as 0.058333. AssemblyAI ships ONE id for two tiers at two rates: $0.21/hour async and $0.45/hour streaming. The id alone does not say which endpoint the caller used, so this catalog splits them, taking the bare id for async and inventing a `-streaming` suffix for the other. That mirrors what it already does for Deepgram, where `nova-3-batch` is a catalog id Deepgram does not ship either. The bare id resolving to the cheaper async rate is a deliberate choice, not a default: it matches the parameter name AssemblyAI documents for the async API (`speech_models`), and a realtime caller has to name the endpoint they are on anyway.

models.name: Universal-3.5 Pro Realtime (streaming)
models.comments: Source rate $0.45/hour, "Universal-3.5 Pro Realtime" under the Streaming Speech-to-Text API tab, which is not the page default and needs a click to reach. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.45 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.125 exactly. Three times the cost of the Universal-Streaming tier ($0.15/hour) and more than double the same model on the async endpoint ($0.21/hour). Reading the async tab and assuming the rate carries over to streaming understates a realtime agent's bill by 2.1x.

models.name: Universal-Streaming English
models.comments: Source rate $0.15/hour, listed on the pricing page under Streaming-Speech-to-Text API as "Universal-Streaming: High-quality realtime model for English only transcription". Converted to $/k seconds: 0.15 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.0416666 recurring, stored as 0.041667. Base rate only; add-on features are priced separately and are not modelled here. Same figure as the async universal-2 tier, arrived at independently: AssemblyAI prices both at $0.15/hour.

models.name: Universal-Streaming Multilingual
models.comments: Source rate $0.15/hour, listed on the pricing page under Streaming-Speech-to-Text API as "Universal-Streaming Multilingual: Multilingual transcription at the speed and cost of Universal-Streaming". Converted to $/k seconds: 0.15 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.0416666 recurring, stored as 0.041667. Unlike most vendors, AssemblyAI charges no multilingual premium here: Deepgram, by contrast, charges about 20% more for Nova-3 multilingual than monolingual.

models.name: Amazon Transcribe (streaming)
models.comments: Source rate $0.0001667 per second (`USE1-StreamingAudio`), equivalently $0.01/minute. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.0001667 * 1000 = 0.1667. Standard transcription is flat, not tiered: the price list carries a single 0-Inf band for this SKU, and the pricing page's own worked example multiplies 2,000,000 minutes by a flat $0.01 with no tier arithmetic. The tiered tables on that page are the add-ons (PII redaction, custom language models, toxicity detection) and Call Analytics, none of which are priced here. Billed in one-second increments with no minimum. A two-channel conversation is billed on total duration, not per channel.

models.name: Amazon Transcribe (batch)
models.comments: Source rate $0.0001 per second (`USE1-TranscribeAudio`), equivalently $0.006/minute. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.0001 * 1000 = 0.1. Flat, for the same reason as `transcribe`. Not modelled: Transcribe Medical, Call Analytics, and the add-on features, which are separately metered.

models.name: Azure Speech to Text (real-time)
models.comments: Source rate $1 per hour, the "Speech to Text / Standard Transcription / Real-time Transcription" row of the pay-as-you-go table. Converted to $/k seconds: 1 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.2777777 recurring, stored as 0.277778 (equivalently $0.0166667/min). Billed per second. Not modelled: Custom Transcription ($1.20/hour), endpoint hosting ($0.0538 per model per hour), Custom Speech training ($10 per compute hour), the enhanced add-on features (language identification, diarization, pronunciation assessment, $0.30 per hour per feature in real-time), the free F0 tier's 5 audio hours a month, and the commitment tiers. Also not priced here: Voice Live, which bills per token rather than per second and is a different product from Speech to Text.

models.name: Azure Speech to Text (batch)
models.comments: Source rate $0.18 per hour, the "Batch Transcription" figure in the same Standard Transcription row. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.18 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.05 (equivalently $0.003/min). Batch includes continuous language identification and diarization at no extra charge, which cost $0.30 per hour per feature in real-time.

models.name: Ink-2
models.comments: Cartesia publishes no per-second rate for STT, only hours included per plan. The credit cost is derived from those and is consistent across all four: 20K credits / 1h51m, 100K / 9h16m, 1.25M / 115h44m, 8M / 740h44m all give 3.00 credits per second of audio. Converted to $/k seconds at the Pro credit price: 3 * 0.00005 * 1000 = 0.15 (equivalently $0.009 per minute).

models.name: Base (legacy)
models.comments: Source rate $0.87/hour, published by Deepgram in the pricing-page FAQ: "These remain available at unchanged rates for existing deployments: Nova-2 streaming at $0.35/hour, Enhanced at $0.99/hour, and Base at $0.87/hour." Converted to $/k seconds: 0.87 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.2416666 recurring, stored as 0.241667. One tier rate covers every domain variant; the FAQ prices the tier and the main rate tables do not list Base at all. No streaming/prerecorded split is published for this tier, so unlike nova-3 there is no `-batch` row. The bare domain ids (`phonecall`, `meeting`) are deliberately NOT added to the provider-level `model_match`: they are too generic to claim for Deepgram from a bare model_ref. They resolve when `provider_id='deepgram'` is supplied, which is how a voice runtime names them.

models.name: Enhanced (legacy)
models.comments: Source rate $0.99/hour, from the same pricing-page FAQ answer that publishes the Base and Nova-2 legacy rates. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.99 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.275 exactly. Worth noting this legacy tier costs more than every current model: Nova-3 monolingual streaming is $0.29/hour and prerecorded $0.26/hour. Enhanced is priced where it was when it was current, which is why Deepgram recommends new projects start on Nova-3.

models.name: Flux (streaming)
models.comments: Source rate $0.0065/minute, the "Current price" for Flux English under Streaming, Pay As You Go. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.0065 * 1000 / 60 ~= 0.108333. Read the CURRENT price, not the "Regular price" $0.0077/minute printed beside it. Deepgram is running a limited-time streaming promotion and each streaming cell shows both numbers; $0.0065 is what is charged today. The FAQ agrees: "Flux ... runs $0.39/hour monolingual", which is $0.0065/minute. There is deliberately no `flux-general-batch`. One existed until 2026-08-20 holding $0.0077/minute, which was the regular streaming price misread as a prerecorded rate. Deepgram's Pre-Recorded table lists only Nova-3 Monolingual, Nova-3 Multilingual, Whisper Large and Custom; Flux has never been on it.

models.name: Nova-2 (streaming)
models.comments: Source rate $0.35/hour, published by Deepgram in the pricing-page FAQ: "These remain available at unchanged rates for existing deployments: Nova-2 streaming at $0.35/hour, Enhanced at $0.99/hour, and Base at $0.87/hour." Converted to $/k seconds: 0.35 / 3600 * 1000 = 0.0972222 recurring, stored as 0.097222. This replaces 0.098333, which came from third-party trackers quoting $0.0059/minute while this row carried a "verify before relying on it" note. Deepgram's own figure works out to $0.0058333/minute, so the old rate was about 1.1% high. Nova-2 is still absent from the main rate tables; the FAQ is now the vendor's published source for it.

models.name: Nova-2 (batch)
models.comments: Source rate $0.0043/minute (prerecorded). Converted to $/k seconds: 0.0043 * 1000 / 60 ~= 0.071667. Unresolved as of 2026-08-20: this is the only Deepgram row still with no vendor source. The pricing FAQ publishes Nova-2 STREAMING ($0.35/hour) but says nothing about prerecorded. Note that $0.0043/minute is also exactly Nova-3 Monolingual's prerecorded rate, so this figure may have been taken from the Nova-3 row rather than a Nova-2 one, the same way the nova-3-batch and flux-general-batch rates were taken from the wrong column. It is left unchanged because there is no evidence either way, and replacing one unsourced number with another would not be an improvement.

models.name: Nova-3 (monolingual batch)

The archived pricing page from 2026-05-31, the day this row was written, already showed $0.0043 under Pre-Recorded, so the rate was wrong when recorded rather than having drifted since. The tell was that batch cost 60% more than streaming ($0.0077 against $0.0048), which is backwards; `test_batch_rates` now asserts the ordering.

models.name: GPT-4o mini Transcribe
models.comments: Token rates are the bill: $1.25/1M text input, $3/1M audio input, $5/1M output. input_audio_kseconds is NOT a billing rate. OpenAI prints $0.003/minute for this model in a column headed "Estimated cost", derived from an assumed speech density, alongside the token rates that are actually charged. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.003 * 1000 / 60 = 0.05 exactly. It is recorded because a voice runtime measures seconds and would otherwise get a silent $0 here, and flagged in provenance.estimated_fields because a caller reconciling against an OpenAI invoice must use the token rates instead. The two meters will not agree: which one is closer depends on how fast the speaker talks, and OpenAI does not publish the tokens-per-minute assumption behind the estimate.

models.name: GPT-4o Transcribe
models.comments: Token rates are the bill: $2.50/1M text input, $6/1M audio input, $10/1M output. input_audio_kseconds is NOT a billing rate. OpenAI prints $0.006/minute for this model in a column headed "Estimated cost", derived from an assumed speech density, alongside the token rates that are actually charged. Converted to $/k seconds: 0.006 * 1000 / 60 = 0.1 exactly. It is recorded because a voice runtime measures seconds and would otherwise get a silent $0 here, and flagged in provenance.estimated_fields because a caller reconciling against an OpenAI invoice must use the token rates instead. Note the collision with whisper-1, which carries the same 0.1 for a different reason: there $0.006/minute is the billed meter and the value is exact, so whisper-1 has no estimated_fields entry. Identical numbers, different standing. gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize shares this row; the pricing page lists no separate rate.

models.name: GPT Live Transcribe
models.comments: Source rate $0.017 per minute, listed on the model page as "Realtime audio duration / Per minute". Converted to $/k seconds: 0.017 * 1000 / 60 = 0.2833333 recurring, stored rounded to six decimal places as 0.283333, matching the other per-minute conversions in this catalog. A one-hour call prices $1.0199988 against $1.02 billed. This is the billed meter, not a derived estimate. The pricing table publishes "-" in both the input and output token columns for this model, and the section is headed "Prices per 1M tokens unless noted", so the per-minute figure is what is noted. Contrast gpt-4o-transcribe, which publishes token rates AND a per-minute figure; there the tokens are the bill and the minute is OpenAI's own estimate. Audio is input only, so the whole rate belongs to input_audio_kseconds.

models.name: GPT-Realtime-Translate
models.comments: Source rate $0.034 per minute, listed on the model page as "Realtime audio duration / Per minute". Converted to $/k seconds: 0.034 * 1000 / 60 = 0.5666666 recurring, stored as 0.566667. The page states it outright: "priced by audio duration rather than text tokens." No token rate is published. Caveat: this model outputs audio as well as taking it in, yet only one duration meter is published, so which direction it measures is not stated. Recorded against input_audio_kseconds because OpenAI uses the identical metric name on gpt-live-transcribe and gpt-realtime-whisper, where audio is input only and the meter can therefore only mean input duration. If OpenAI clarifies that it meters both directions, revisit this rather than silently doubling it.

models.comments: Source rate $0.017 per minute, listed on the model page as "Realtime audio duration / Per minute". The model page states outright: "GPT-Realtime-Whisper is priced by audio duration rather than text tokens." No token rate is published, so there is no second meter and nothing here is an estimate. Audio is input only. Same rate as gpt-live-transcribe; the two are separate model ids, so both are listed.

Audio is input only, so the whole rate belongs to input_audio_kseconds. Note this is a different model from gpt-4o-transcribe ($0.006/min estimated, billed per token) and roughly a third cheaper.

models.name: Standard
